newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money slips amid ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: German call money slips amid ample liquidity.

text.p: German call money rates nudged slightly lower to trade around 2.98/3.00 percent on Thursday as liquidity conditions remain ample ahead of month-end.
Dealers explained that this week's more generous than expected 3.5 billion mark injection into the money market helped supply the market with ample, although not excessive, liquidity.
Banks have since improved their reserve holdings ahead of this month's larger than usual tax payment date, leading dealers to predict relatively calm month-end dealings.
Banks held 41.8 billion marks on Wednesday compared with 39.3 billion a day earlier while the average holdings climbed to 38.5 billion marks from 38.3 billion marks.
Lombard borrowings were neglible on Wednesday, the Bundesbank said.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.04408 percent on Thursday compared with 3.05200 percent on Wednesday.
